newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks down on inflation, property woes.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks down on inflation, property woes.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed lower on Thursday for the first time in four days, as inflation and property market fears undermined sentiment, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index was down 67.98 points or 0.55 percent at 12,358.7. Turnover was HK$8.18 billion, significantly higher compared with Wednedsay's HK$6.66 billion.

"Basically, (it's) East Point -- 52 units only taken up out of 215," said James Osborn, sales director at Barings, adding that Sun Hung Kai's East Point sale on Wednesday had compounded bearish comments by Henderson.
Wall Street and the property sector jitters took the heart out of local investors on Thursday afternoon, at one time pushing the Hang Seng Index down more than 100 points.
"I think they're (Wall Street and the property market) both combining to create a poor sentiment at this time," said Grant Forster, vice president BT Fund Managers.
Rory McAllister at HSBC James Capel's institutional sales said the sale of a Henderson Land Metro City development would "roughly confirm" whether Hong Kong's property prices were dipping.
Investors were looking for more China plays, red chips, and even some H shares such as Maanshan, said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager with Nikko Securities.
Shares in red chip Shanghai Industrial closed up HK$0.30 at HK$35.80 after a placement of 139.47 million new shares to fund the purchase of China assets.
China Light shares surged HK$1.00 to HK$34.50 on the news that it had signed a joint venture agreement with Exxon Energy to build a plant in China's Shenzhen.
Shares in China Light's 20 percent shareholder, red chip, CITIC Pacific, fell HK$0.20 to HK$37.70.
China Resources fell HK$0.05 to HK$17.35.
In the property sector Sun Hung Kai led the losses, falling $1.00 to HK$76.50, while New World Development lost HK$0.98 to HK$40.30.
Wharf ended HK$0.60 lower at HK$30.70, and sister company Wheelock fell HK$0.35 to $16.80.
Shares in Sino Land, which plans a convertible bond issue for working capital and property activities, fell HK$0.20 to HK$7.40.
Among the banks, HSBC lost HK$0.50 to HK$181, while Dah Sing lost HK$0.88 to HK$31.00.
